action_items: Fix BIFF drawer Escape regression: in TrapModal add onEscapeKeyDown={(e) => e.stopPropagation()} on Dialog.Content (Radix calls it from its document capture listener, so the DrawerShell window keydown listener never sees the Escape). Stopping propagation does not block other Radix layers on document (court dialog still checks isHighestLayer). Alternatively make DrawerShell skip Escape when e.defaultPrevented. Then retest nav-biff -> raw-input -> Escape (notice and confirm) and the court chat Escape.
critical_code_review_comments: AiNoticeModals.jsx: stopEscape on Content onKeyDown no longer works: Radix closes the dialog in a document capture listener, React unmounts it before the bubble phase, so the React handler never runs and the native event reaches window listeners (DrawerShell). This causes the regression above.

AiNoticeProvider: Enter/typing on a locked box (focused by keyboard after Escape) does nothing silently; the pop-up only reopens on click/focus. Acceptable, but a keydown->openNotice on locked inputs would help keyboard users.

rca of the issue: BIFF drawer Escape: TrapModal moved to @radix-ui/react-dialog. Radix DismissableLayer handles Escape in a document keydown CAPTURE listener and calls onOpenChange(false) -> setNoticeOpen(false). The React update runs in the microtask after that listener, so the dialog content unmounts before the target/bubble phase. The onKeyDown={stopEscape} handler on Dialog.Content then never runs, and the native keydown bubbles to window, where DrawerShell (JourneyDrawers.jsx line ~38) calls onClose(). Repro: reset parent1 AI notice, 390px, / -> nav-biff -> tap raw-input -> Escape -> drawer gone. Fix: stopPropagation inside Radix onEscapeKeyDown.
